headline: High: Continue can write and inspect workspace files while dbt-core can act on warehouse data, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue reads and writes workspace files and uses MCP/tooling, so attacker-controlled content in shared files can influence its instructions. dbt-core consumes warehouse-facing inputs/outputs, so if Continue writes prompts or instructions into shared artifacts that dbt-core later reads, the pair has a plausible injection bridge. The shared filesystem path is documented; no provenance guard is shown.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or artifact directory, injected text can cross from Continue to dbt-core.
IF dbt-core consumes files produced by Continue without provenance checks, prompt-like content can be treated as instructions.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Disable MCP servers not needed for the task.
Require a human review step before dbt-core consumes any file written by Continue.
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts where possible.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and content-type validation between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and has broad network egress; dbt-core touches data warehouse data and also has network access to the warehouse. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive code or warehouse-derived data can flow between them through files or outputs. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so the default risk is material but not proven catastrophic.
conditions: IF the same workspace contains source code and warehouse artifacts, Continue can read both.
IF dbt-core writes warehouse-derived outputs into the shared filesystem, Continue can read them back.
IF either agent is configured with shared credentials, data can traverse the pair unintentionally.
mitigations: Use separate service accounts and credentials.
Keep warehouse outputs out of the IDE workspace.
Restrict Continue to least-privilege file access.
Rotate any shared secrets after testing the pair.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and DLP controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue can execute shell commands, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem; dbt-core can call warehouse APIs. Those overlapping mutation surfaces can conflict if both operate on the same project state or generated artifacts. The profiles do not show locking or coordination primitives, so concurrent writes or stale reads are plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same project files or generated artifacts, race conditions can occur.
IF Continue installs packages while dbt-core runs against the same environment, dependency drift can break runs.
IF the orchestrator provides no locking, concurrent mutations can interleave.
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time.
Pin dependencies before concurrent use.
Use separate virtual environments.
Add file locks around generated artifacts.
requires-engineering: introduce orchestration-level locking and transaction boundaries.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or instructions from editor context, and dbt-core can act on warehouse data and project files. If dbt-core treats Continue's output as authoritative, a mistaken transformation or prompt-induced hallucination can cascade into incorrect models, broken pipelines, or committed bad SQL. Because the pair lacks a documented verification gate, the default pathway is dangerous.
conditions: IF dbt-core consumes Continue-generated SQL or instructions without validation, errors can propagate downstream.
IF Continue produces incorrect facts about schema or data, dbt-core can operationalize them.
IF the workflow auto-runs transformations after generation, the blast radius expands to multiple work products.
mitigations: Require explicit review before execution.
Validate generated SQL against tests.
Compare outputs against schema metadata.
Limit auto-run workflows.
requires-engineering: add semantic checks and rollback for downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Continue handles source code and open editor buffers, while dbt-core handles data warehouse data. If warehouse data includes regulated or residency-bound records, the pair can create a compliance mismatch when Continue's broad egress or local workspace handling exposes data outside the warehouse controls. No specific certifications or residency guarantees are documented for either agent, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated records, Continue may expose them through the IDE workspace.
IF the warehouse is subject to residency or retention rules, exporting artifacts into the shared workspace can violate policy.
IF logs or prompts retain sensitive snippets, retention mismatches can occur.
mitigations: Exclude regulated tables from the workflow.
Mask sensitive fields before sharing artifacts.
Review retention settings for both tools.
Keep compliance-bound data out of editor buffers.
requires-engineering: document residency, retention, and DPA boundaries.
